summary: Registers the media type application/rdf+xml for the XML serialization of the Resource Description Framework. RDF supports the Semantic Web by providing structures for describing resources and exchanging data about them.

eli5.summary: Files full of facts about things need a name tag so computers know what they are. This document registers the tag for one such kind.

questions: what is the application/rdf+xml mime type
how do rdf/xml documents get labeled
subtitle: Official registration of the application/rdf+xml MIME type for semantic web documents.

tldr.problem: Resource Description Framework (RDF) documents in XML format need a registered MIME type so software can automatically recognize and parse them correctly.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3870 registers the media type application/rdf+xml according to MIME registration procedures, specifying the character encoding rules, file extensions, and how fragment identifiers work.
tldr.outcome: Software receiving a file labeled with application/rdf+xml knows it contains semantic web data in XML format and can process it accordingly. RDF documents can be reliably exchanged over HTTP and email.

today: RFC 3870 is an Informational RFC that completes the media type registration begun in RFC 3023. The application/rdf+xml type remains the standard way to label RDF/XML documents. This RFC has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: RDF and the Semantic Web
sections.content:
The Resource Description Framework (RDF) is a language for describing resources and their properties in a way machines can understand. Instead of just text like 'John knows Mary', RDF lets you say 'the person with URI http://example.org/john has a knows property pointing to http://example.org/mary'. This structured, machine-readable format powers the Semantic Web, where data is explicitly linked and can be automatically processed.

RDF can be written in several formats. The W3C defined RDF/XML syntax, which expresses RDF data as XML. An RDF/XML document is valid XML that contains resource descriptions. When such a document is sent over HTTP or email, software needs to know it is RDF/XML to process it correctly. This RFC registers the MIME type application/rdf+xml for that purpose.
sections.eli5: RDF is a way to write facts that computers can understand. This RFC gives it a label (MIME type) so that when you send an RDF file to someone, their computer automatically knows what to do with it.

sections.title: MIME Type Registration Details
sections.content:
The formal registration specifies several key properties. The media type is application/rdf+xml, with no required parameters. An optional charset parameter specifies character encoding, following the same rules as application/xml (per RFC 3023). RDF/XML documents should use the RFC/XML Syntax Grammar (the newer specification) rather than the older RDF Model and Syntax.

RDF documents do not have a magic byte sequence that uniquely identifies them, but they will contain the RDF namespace URI http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#, usually near the top. The recommended file extension is .rdf, and the Macintosh file type code is 'rdf '. The intended usage is COMMON, meaning this media type is expected to see wide use.
sections.eli5: When you send an RDF/XML file, add the label 'application/rdf+xml'. You can say what language it is (like UTF-8). Files should end in .rdf. Computers will recognize the RDF namespace inside to confirm it is really RDF.

sections.title: Fragment Identifiers and Semantic Implications
sections.content:
In a URL, the fragment identifier (the part after '#') normally refers to a specific location in a document. In RDF, fragments are more semantically complex. The RDF attributes rdf:ID and rdf:about define fragments in an RDF document. However, in RDF the thing identified by a URI with a fragment identifier (e.g., http://example.org/doc#john) does not necessarily relate to the document itself in simple ways; it refers to the named resource.

This differs from some interpretations of the URI specification and requires careful handling when creating new RDF terms using fragment identifiers. Applications must understand that the semantic relationship between the base URI and the fragment is defined by RDF semantics, not by document structure.
sections.eli5: When you use a '#' in an RDF URL, it doesn't point to a spot in the file like it usually does. It points to a thing that the RDF describes. Be careful when you write RDF with '#' in the names.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
RDF is a generic format for exchanging information and does not itself provide security. The security considerations for XML (from RFC 3023) apply equally to RDF/XML documents. RDF data can be secured using any mechanism available for XML or MIME, including XML Signature, XML Encryption, S/MIME, OpenPGP, or transport-level security (TLS).

A deeper security concern is that RDF is designed to make assertions about anything and to combine information from many sources. This means RDF applications can make false assertions either by direct statement or by logical deduction. Application designers must not assume RDF provides correctness guarantees. The formal semantics of RDF can help track provenance (where information comes from), but designers must always apply skepticism to combined information and understand the reliability of their sources.
sections.eli5: RDF files can contain lies or mistakes. Just because a file says something is true doesn't mean it is. If you combine RDF data from multiple sources, you might end up with contradictions or false conclusions. Always think about where your data comes from.
